# ParBayesianOptimization 1.4.2

After the back to CRAN release of 
[ParBayesianOptimization](/posts/2026-09-20-parbayesianoptimization-is-back-on-cran) 
v1.4.2 is the first release that reaches users with some new features.


ParBayesianOptimization is a package that tunes model hyperparameters with Bayesian
optimization: it fits a Gaussian process to the scores you have so far and
uses it to pick the next parameters to try, optionally running your scoring
function in parallel.

This release focuses on a lighter install and on making long, unattended runs
behave predictably. You can see a full list of changes in the
release notes for [1.4.2](https://github.com/novica/ParBayesianOptimization/releases/tag/v1.4.2).

## A much lighter install

Installing 1.3.0 pulled in 84 packages, including stringi and most of the
tidyverse, all to arrange two scatter plots. ggpubr is now replaced by
patchwork and crayon by cli, which brings the count down to 27.

This matters most where ParBayesianOptimization usually runs: on servers,
in Docker images and on HPC nodes, where every extra compiled dependency is
something to build, cache and keep working.

The new dependencies do require R 4.1 or later, as ggplot2 and lhs already
do.

`plot()` draws the same two panels as before, with the score of each run on
top and the utility the Gaussian process expected from it below. It now
returns a patchwork object, and any arguments you pass go to
`patchwork::plot_layout()`, where they override the defaults. For example,
to put the panels side by side:

```r
plot(optObj, ncol = 2)
```

If you saved or modified the object returned by `plot()` in 1.3.0, which
was a ggpubr `ggarrange` object, check that code: patchwork objects work
with `ggsave()` and `&`/`+` theming, but `ggarrange()` arguments such as
`common.legend` are no longer accepted.

## No more prompts in unattended runs

`addIterations()` lets you continue an optimization, optionally with new
bounds. If you tightened the bounds so that some earlier results fell
outside them, 1.3.0 stopped and asked `Continue? [y/n]` with `readline()`.
That's fine at the console, but in a batch job or on a cluster nobody is
there to answer.

Now it warns instead, and leaves those results out of the Gaussian
process fit:

```r
optObj <- addIterations(optObj, bounds = list(x = c(2, 10)), iters.n = 5)
#> Warning message:
#> Bounds have been tightened. 1 parameter set in scoreSummary is outside
#> the new bounds and will be ignored this round.
```

Two related fixes make this reliable: the first Gaussian process fit in
`addIterations()` now also leaves out-of-bounds rows out, and the check for
"enough samples to fit" counts only error-free results within the bounds.

## Catching mistakes before `FUN` runs

Your scoring function is usually the expensive part, often a full
cross-validated model fit. Mistakes that only surface after it has run cost
real time.

Arguments in `...` are passed to `DiceKriging::km()`, which fits the
Gaussian process. In 1.3.0 a typo there was only caught when the first
Gaussian process was fitted, after the initial scoring runs had finished.
Now `bayesOpt()`, `addIterations()` and `updateGP()` check them up front:

```r
bayesOpt(FUN, bounds, initPoints = 4, nugget.extimate = TRUE)
#> Error in checkKmArgs(...):
#>   Arguments in ... are passed to DiceKriging::km(), which does not
#>   accept: nugget.extimate. Check for misspelled arguments.
```

Unique prefixes of `km()` arguments are still accepted, just as R accepts
them.

The acquisition function is also validated more strictly. `acq` must be a
single string, and its options now appear in the `bayesOpt()` signature, so
your editor can show them:

```r
bayesOpt(..., acq = c("ucb", "ei", "eips", "poi"))
```

`"ucb"` stays the default.

## What's next

I plan to make another release before New Year, but hopefully I can get some
feedback before. The development version already has some changes for using 
`cli` throughout the package. 

The remaining heavy dependency is ggplot2 itself, again only for `plot()`.
I am thinking that a package like this should not pull so many depedencies 
just to draw one plot. [Issue #48](https://github.com/novica/ParBayesianOptimization/issues/48)
proposes drawing the plot with tinyplot instead, which would bring the
count down to 11 packages. It changes what `plot()` returns, so feedback is
welcome there before it goes into a release.
